themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 302 THIS WEEK—a 515% spike versus the 49.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 18.61)—signaling a sudden, severe deterioration in road conditions across Queens Village/Cambria Heights that demands immediate investigation into cause and city response.
evidence: 302 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 49.1 weekly average (515% increase, z-score: 18.61)
Street condition is #2 complaint category overall (1,428 over 90 days), but acceleration is exclusively recent
Community Board has repeatedly requested street reconstruction funding—suggest underlying systemic issues now surfacing
reporting_angles: Photo essay: map and document worst-hit blocks; interview DOT about emergency repairs and timeline
Investigate whether recent weather, construction, or deferred maintenance triggered the spike
Interview residents on impact: commute delays, vehicle damage, pedestrian safety risks

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Overgrowth Surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints spiked to 46 THIS WEEK (360% above 10.0 weekly average) and overgrown tree/branches complaints hit 13 THIS WEEK (197% above 4.4 weekly average), suggesting storm damage, disease, or neglected Parks Department maintenance now creating safety hazards.
evidence: 46 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.0 weekly average (360% spike, z-score: 6.13)
13 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average (197% spike, z-score: 6.12)
Community Board has standing request for better park maintenance—suggests chronic underfunding now manifesting
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm or weather event that caused limb breakage? Document locations and damage severity.
Interview Parks Dept on tree inspection frequency and maintenance backlog in CD 413
Safety angle: are broken branches or overgrowth blocking sidewalks or creating pedestrian hazards?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Cleanliness Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped to 31 THIS WEEK (176% spike versus 11.2 weekly average, z-score: 5.72) and dirty condition complaints hit 39 last week (176% spike versus 14.1 average), indicating rapid deterioration in street and public space hygiene.
evidence: 31 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.2 weekly average (176% increase, z-score: 5.72)
39 dirty condition complaints last week vs. 14.1 weekly average (176% increase, z-score: 3.86)
Dead animal complaints also spiked to 13 last week (225% above 4.0 average), suggesting potential public health vector
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: visit high-complaint areas to document conditions; photograph and geolocate problem spots
Interview Sanitation Dept: is there a collection schedule disruption, staffing shortage, or service reduction?
Public health angle: do elevated dead animal and unsanitary complaints suggest disease vector or pest infestation risk?

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Malfunction Wave
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints jumped to 76 last week (144% spike versus 31.1 weekly average, z-score: 3.59), a sharp escalation that could affect commuter safety and traffic flow across the district.
evidence: 76 traffic signal complaints last week vs. 31.1 weekly average (144% spike, z-score: 3.59)
Traffic signal condition is #9 complaint category overall (561 over 90 days), but spike is recent and sharp
Correlates with street condition spike, suggesting possible weather or infrastructure damage event
reporting_angles: Interview DOT on signal outages: scope, cause (weather, accidents, maintenance?), and repair timeline
Safety impact reporting: have traffic collisions increased? Interview NYPD on recent accident reports near malfunctioning signals
Map complaint locations to identify geographic cluster and priority intersections

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Blocked Driveway Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 49 two weeks ago (372% above 10.4 weekly average, z-score: 8.98), compounding the district's chronic blocked driveway issue (1,061 complaints over 90 days), suggesting parking enforcement breakdown or infrastructure debris.
evidence: 49 obstruction complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 10.4 weekly average (372% spike, z-score: 8.98)
Blocked driveway complaints remain chronically high at 1,061 over 90 days (#4 complaint category)
Illegal parking also high at 1,846 complaints—suggests enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Investigate whether obstruction spike was weather-related debris (fallen branches, garbage) or illegal parking
Interview NYPD Parking Enforcement on staffing and ticketing patterns in CD 413; any recent changes?
Resident interviews: how long are residents blocked? What is impact on emergency response times?
